title: Filtered Cartan--Eilenberg comparison with truncation spectral object
statement: Let A, B and C be Grothendieck abelian categories with derived categories, and F : A to B and G : B to C additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix a functor E to E₂ cohomological spectral sequences and object isomorphisms c_X to the truncation spectral sequence of RG(RF(X)), such that their canonical page-two comparisons with H^{p+q}(RG(tau_{>=q} tau_{<q+1} RF(X))) are natural for all integer p,q. Then there exist a common filtered page-two model M [def-sp-filtered-page-two-model], filtrations L_P on each mapped CE total [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], and isomorphisms s_P : E(P.X) ≅ M.S(Tot G(P.I),L_P). Each L_P agrees degreewise with the second filtration [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Every presentation comparison d admits a filtered lift t whose underlying map is Tot G(d.alpha), and E(d.f) s_Q = s_P M.S(t).

proof.text: Construct the quotient-image spectral sequence on all filtered complexes by the three adjacent total-degree kernel/image constructions, with differential induced by the original complex differential. The kernel/cokernel equations produce coherent homology isomorphisms and natural maps, yielding M. Use the second filtration and comparison independence to obtain the required filtrations and filtered total lifts.

Before G is applied, put Dec(V)^a Tot(I)^n = V^(a+n) intersect d^{-1}(V^(a+n+1)). The augmentation of tau_{<=q} F(J) lies in Dec(V)^(-q), by resolution degree zero below q and the cycle condition at q. The CE cycle, boundary and cohomology resolutions identify its graded augmentation as a quasi-isomorphism. Injectivity splits the horizontal cycle/boundary sequences; finite sums of their terms give injective graded Dec terms and split steps, hence a filtered injective resolution of the truncation filtration.

Apply the filtered injective comparison of Stacks 015X to this filtered injective resolution. Additivity of G preserves comparison homotopies. The Dec cycle and boundary formulas shift pages once, and reindexing gives the second-filtration spectral sequence from page two. Original complex differentials on representatives and quotient homology compute both constructions, so the comparison respects the spectral-sequence differentials and homology isomorphisms.

The split horizontal cohomology computation identifies page-two comparison maps with the maps of the truncation spectral object; (-1)^(q*j) normalizes resolution differential signs. The assumed naturality of c gives the page-two square with E(f). Inductively, spectral-sequence morphisms are determined by page two through their successor-page homology isomorphisms, so that square holds on every page. Compose with c to obtain s; use the filtered lift already constructed for each presentation comparison.
